terms-of-service.title: Terms of service
terms-of-service.excerpt: Proposed RMDHost service terms covering orders, billing, responsibilities, cancellation, security and service commitments.
terms-of-service.html:
Draft for review · 15 October 2026. These proposed policies require RMDHost approval before taking effect. Your accepted order and applicable mandatory law remain authoritative.

TermsPrivacyAcceptable useFair useSLACookies

1. Provider and scope

These proposed terms cover RMDHost virtual servers, dedicated servers, storage and game hosting. The contracting entity, registered address and applicable jurisdiction must be identified in the accepted order. For questions, contact support@rmdhost.com.

2. Orders and service descriptions

An order should identify the product, resources, location, billing currency, fees, support scope and any special commitments. A catalogue entry is subject to stock and confirmation. Services marked Coming Soon cannot be purchased through that entry. Third-party checkout sites have their own terms; review the identity of the seller before paying.

3. Accounts and access

Provide accurate account and billing details, keep credentials secure and notify support promptly about unauthorised access. You are responsible for people you authorise to use your account and for appropriate access controls on your services.

4. Billing and renewal

The order specifies billing frequency, renewal date and any setup or licence charges. Applicable taxes and the final total must be disclosed before payment. GBP estimates of supplier USD prices are indicative; the checkout currency and accepted total govern. Any payment failure, suspension or cancellation process must follow the accepted order and applicable law.

5. Permitted use and management

Follow our Acceptable Use Policy and Fair Use Policy. Unless management is included in the order, customers administer their software, patches, firewall, content and application configuration. Support availability does not mean software management is included.

6. Backups and customer data

Maintain independent backups and test recovery. If a plan includes backup, confirm its schedule, retention and restore procedure. File synchronisation, RAID and DDoS filtering are not substitutes for backup. On cancellation, export data before the service deletion date stated in your order.

7. Availability and incidents

Any binding uptime commitment and service-credit entitlement must be stated in the accepted order or agreed SLA. Marketing figures are not evidence of measured uptime. Planned work, incidents and urgent security measures may affect availability.

8. Cancellation and refunds

Use the client area or contact support to request cancellation. Confirm the effective date, renewal cutoff and data-export deadline. Refund eligibility, statutory cancellation rights and non-refundable third-party charges must be disclosed before purchase. No blanket refund window is established by this draft.

9. Abuse and suspension

We may need to restrict an affected service to address illegal activity, compromised systems or immediate harm. Where practical, explain the issue and give an opportunity to respond. Mandatory legal orders and urgent incidents may require action before notice.

10. Liability, disputes and changes

Any liability cap, exclusions and governing law require confirmation in the final agreement. Nothing in the final terms may exclude rights or liabilities that applicable law protects. Contact support first to attempt resolution. Material changes should be communicated before they take effect, with any required notice or cancellation rights.

privacy-policy.title: Privacy policy
privacy-policy.excerpt: Proposed RMDHost privacy notice describing account data, technical logs, support records, cookies, processors and individual rights.
privacy-policy.html:
Draft for review · 15 October 2026. These proposed policies require RMDHost approval before taking effect. Your accepted order and applicable mandatory law remain authoritative.

TermsPrivacyAcceptable useFair useSLACookies

1. Who handles your data

RMDHost uses account and technical information to operate hosting services. The final notice must identify the legal controller and its address. Privacy enquiries can be sent to support@rmdhost.com. Hosting customers may separately act as controllers for data they store on their servers; an appropriate processing agreement is needed where we act as processor.

2. Information involved

Depending on how you interact with us, information may include name, contact and billing details, order history, transaction references, IP addresses, security logs, device or browser details, support correspondence and consent preferences. Avoid sending passwords or unnecessary sensitive information in tickets. Payment processors handle payment credentials under their own notices.

3. Purposes and legal grounds

Account setup, provisioning, billing and support are needed to perform the service contract. Security and abuse prevention may rely on legitimate interests, subject to applicable safeguards. Accounting and lawful disclosures may be legal obligations. Where required, optional analytics or marketing relies on consent. The final notice must match actual tools and processing.

4. Sharing and third parties

Infrastructure providers, payment processors and support or communications providers may receive the information necessary for their role. Information may also be disclosed where legally required. External supplier checkout and account websites are operated separately; review their privacy notices before using them. The final notice must identify relevant recipient categories and processing arrangements.

5. Cookies and external resources

Read the Cookie Policy and use cookie settings to manage optional consent. The website may request external fonts, which can disclose IP and browser information to the font provider. Disabling optional analytics does not remove necessary service or security processing.

6. International transfers

Server and service locations can involve processing outside your country. Confirm provider locations, subprocessors and any legally required transfer mechanism before moving personal data. This draft does not certify a particular transfer safeguard or residency commitment.

7. Retention and security

Keep personal information only as long as necessary for its purpose, legal obligations or disputes. Specific retention periods, backup deletion cycles and account-deletion procedures must be confirmed in the final notice. Access controls, encryption where appropriate and incident procedures reduce risk but cannot eliminate it.

8. Your rights and requests

Depending on applicable law, you may request access, correction, erasure, restriction or portability, object to processing or withdraw consent. Contact support@rmdhost.com; identity verification may be needed. Rights can have legal exceptions. You may also complain to the competent data protection authority, including the ICO where UK law applies.

9. Children and notice changes

These services are intended for people able to enter the relevant service contract. If a child has supplied personal information without appropriate authority, contact us. The final policy must explain material changes and its effective date.

acceptable-use.title: Acceptable use policy
acceptable-use.excerpt: Proposed acceptable-use rules for RMDHost services covering lawful content, spam, network security and abuse response.
acceptable-use.html:
Draft for review · 15 October 2026. These proposed policies require RMDHost approval before taking effect. Your accepted order and applicable mandatory law remain authoritative.

TermsPrivacyAcceptable useFair useSLACookies

1. Scope

This proposed policy applies to hosting services, customer content and authorised users. Customers must comply with applicable law, the accepted order and relevant software or game licences.

2. Unlawful or harmful material

Do not host or distribute illegal content, child sexual abuse material, malware, stolen credentials or material that infringes others’ rights. Do not use services for fraud, phishing, extortion, exploitation or unlawful disclosure of personal data.

3. Network and system abuse

Do not launch DDoS attacks, compromise other systems, operate malicious command-and-control infrastructure, bypass access restrictions or perform intrusive testing without the affected owner’s permission. Prevent insecure services from becoming amplification sources or open relays.

4. Messaging and spam

Do not send unsolicited bulk messages or operate systems used to distribute spam. Use permission-based lists, maintain consent evidence, respect unsubscribe requests and follow applicable communication laws. Purchased or scraped addresses do not by themselves establish consent.

5. Resource and licence compliance

Stay within contracted allocations and follow the Fair Use Policy. Game files, mods, operating systems and commercial software must be properly licensed. Do not evade product limits or access restrictions.

6. Security duties

Keep software patched, protect administrative access and investigate credible compromise reports. You remain responsible for authorised users and for taking reasonable steps to stop harmful traffic from your service.

7. Reporting and response

Report suspected abuse to support@rmdhost.com with the affected address, timestamps, evidence and your contact details. We assess reports and may request a response, restrict an affected service, preserve relevant records or comply with lawful requests. Where feasible we explain the issue and restoration requirements. Urgent threats can require immediate action.

8. Review and appeal

Contact support if you believe a restriction is mistaken. Provide the service ID, explanation and remediation evidence. The accepted agreement and applicable law govern final enforcement and termination rights.

fair-use.title: Fair use policy
fair-use.excerpt: Proposed fair-use rules explaining shared CPU, unmetered bandwidth, player slots and resource-impact reviews.
fair-use.html:
Draft for review · 15 October 2026. These proposed policies require RMDHost approval before taking effect. Your accepted order and applicable mandatory law remain authoritative.

TermsPrivacyAcceptable useFair useSLACookies

1. Meaning of plan limits

Plan allocations and the accepted order define available CPU, RAM, storage, traffic and ports. Shared resources must be used without materially disrupting other customers. This policy does not change explicitly purchased dedicated allocations.

2. Unmetered is not unlimited speed

Unmetered traffic usually means no stated per-GB billing within the selected port and contract conditions. It is not a promise of uninterrupted line-rate throughput. A port speed, traffic quota and network mitigation capacity are separate specifications.

3. CPU, storage and workloads

Sustained CPU contention, excessive disk I/O, full storage or unusually high packet rates can affect a shared platform. Tell sales about continuous heavy processing, public proxies, high-traffic delivery or similar workloads so suitability can be confirmed before ordering. No arbitrary CPU percentage or daily limit is imposed by this draft.

4. Game-server capacity

Unlimited player slots does not mean unlimited CPU, RAM or guaranteed performance at every player count. Mods, map size, tick rate and simultaneous players influence resource demand. Review the selected game package before inviting a large community.

5. Review process

When activity affects platform stability, support should explain the measured impact and discuss optimisation, an upgrade, traffic controls or a different service. Urgent harm may require temporary restrictions. Any permanent restriction or extra charge must have a contractual basis.

6. Questions and related rules

Ask support@rmdhost.com to confirm suitability for an unusual workload. See the Acceptable Use Policy for prohibited activity and the Terms of Service for contract terms.

sla.title: Service level agreement
sla.excerpt: Proposed RMDHost SLA framework defining network availability measurement, exclusions, incident evidence and credit requests.
sla.html:
Draft for review · 15 October 2026. These proposed policies require RMDHost approval before taking effect. Your accepted order and applicable mandatory law remain authoritative.

TermsPrivacyAcceptable useFair useSLACookies

1. Scope and status

This is a proposed SLA framework. It does not establish a new uptime guarantee or service-credit entitlement. The accepted order must identify the covered service, network boundary, availability target, measurement method and remedy before this agreement takes effect.

2. Network and application availability

Network availability concerns connectivity at the agreed service boundary. Application errors, operating-system failures, game crashes and customer firewall rules are separate unless a managed-service agreement covers them. Support availability is also different from server uptime.

3. How availability is measured

The final agreement should define the monitoring locations, measurement interval, incident start and end, and how conflicting evidence is resolved. A typical calculation is: availability = (eligible measurement minutes minus eligible downtime minutes) ÷ eligible measurement minutes × 100. Define any excluded minutes before applying this formula.

4. Targets and credits

A 100% Network Uptime SLA is a contractual target, not proof of past or future uninterrupted service. No universal RMDHost percentage, credit band or credit cap has been confirmed. Obtain a written service-specific target, credit schedule and claim deadline before purchase; supplier marketing does not automatically transfer a remedy to your order.

5. Maintenance and exclusions

The final SLA must specify how planned maintenance, emergency security work, customer actions, upstream incidents, abuse restrictions and force-majeure events are treated. DDoS events should not be assumed either included or excluded without a written term. Maintenance notice and measurement exclusions require explicit agreement.

6. Reporting and evidence

Open a support ticket promptly with the service ID, affected IP, start and end times including timezone, affected protocols and available logs. Keep monitoring evidence. Engineers can investigate connectivity separately from application health. Never include passwords or secret keys.

7. Credit review

Support reviews the incident against the accepted SLA and confirms qualifying downtime and the applicable remedy. Any credit basis, exclusions, maximum amount, claim deadline and whether credits offset future invoices must be agreed in the final schedule. This draft does not promise a cash refund.

8. Related documents

Read the Terms of Service, DDoS protection details and Acceptable Use Policy. Ask sales to supply an approved SLA for the product and region you intend to order.
